metadata.baseline_note: without_skill baseline intentionally skipped: regression detection plus three new assertions on eval 1.

notes: Eval 1 gained three assertions read from git rather than the working tree: HEAD's contract carries the dated Improvement log entry, nothing about it is left staged, and the commit touching it carries one file. Red->green proven on real runs of the same skill — the pre-T3 run matured and staged (3 FAIL), the post-T3 run matured and committed (7/7, commit f0af9d0 carrying only the contract).

Eval 4 re-run because step 1 changed again (the no-slug listing): the probe still refuses before Rule 1, and the run still leaves data/plate-audits.md byte-intact — the fallback target the fixture keeps in place on purpose.

A dedicated eval 5 was built and then deleted. Its fixture made the contract self-contradictory, which BLOCKS the run, while step 4 matures only after a successful one — so no assertion could have made it test the commit rule. Recorded because the attempt produced the finding below.

FINDING, out of scope and carried to slice 3: two competent executors split on the blocked fixture. One proceeded with the true value and matured the contract; the other refused to emit a non-conforming output AND refused to mature, holding that a schema change with a version bump is not a blocked run's call. The second is right on the skill as written, but the skill says nothing about a run blocked by a defect in its OWN contract.
Both executors declined to publish their HTML report to an artifact URL, citing the workdir-only constraint — the deviation recorded in the v0.49.0 benchmark did not recur.
Counts are the grader's own PASS:/FAIL: lines.
